slides.title: Objective: Share reflections of themes in industry recruitment

runs.t: Objective: Share reflections of themes in industry recruitment

cells: Academia is a safe privileged environment
Wide variety of organizations outside university
There is often time to think and explore ideas
Often there is a revenue/profit motive
For the most part, industry is not like that

runs.t: Many - math graduates who can write code are popular - high endurance, abstraction, creative thinking:
Daily stand up (ritual: team progress, plans, updates & blockers)
Data & communications locked to device, everything monitored
Don’t open whatsapp/fb/instagram/personal email or install programs
Organizations processing big data use cloud:
Amazon AWS, Google GCP, Microsoft Azure, Huawei, Alibaba Cloud
Tech & start-ups are mostly using cloud
Everything will be locked down and visible
Keep communications short and business-like, not too formal
Email is mostly for old economy companies
Shared drive: KB, MB, GB data volume
xslx, tsv, csv, txt, db, sql file formats
GB, PB, XB, YB data volume
Work with servers using Python, SQL (sometimes R, Node, Java)
avro, parquet, orc, json, bson, fasta, fastq, sql file formats
Perks: Massages, Relocation, Healthcare, Education/Travel Budget, Work From Home, Gifts, Food
List out skills relevant to roles that interest you
Have an sharable link (with a tiny url)
Spanish, English (English is really important for many jobs)
Can cost 5-15% of the total budget, 30% of first year salary, 200% to replace a bad hire
Bad hires are a weight on the organization
Serious candidates need to demonstrate motivation
Learn to work in groups of 2-5 people, ideally cross functional teams
Many organizations work on quarterly budgets and allocations
Could apply around the quarters (Dec/Jan, March/April, June/July, Sept/Oct)
Probably best to get to a big city, you’ll learn more quickly working with highly skilled people
Live close to work for the first year (even if it’s a small apartment share)
Work crazy hard for the first 6 months
Don’t mention you want to go back to university (PhD/Masters)
LinkedIn coffee meetings with potential colleagues
Not fair, but filtering is expensive and boring
Be nice (your prospective colleagues will spend more time with you than their partner)
External (not ideal - will eat into your compensation - maybe 30%)
Only a guide (sometimes a senior post, will consider a good junior)
No one completes all the requirements
Work out if the position is in a cost center or revenue driver for the business
Make the resume fit the job
Highlight skills relevant to the jobs
Google then write to the internal recruiter
Write to googled prospective colleagues (LinkedIn, BlueSky, X, Mastodon)
It filters on experience, universities, age, keywords, companies etc
Write to internal recruiters directly, write to prospective colleagues
Understand revenue/profit/cost sources of the organization
Dress code depends on industry sector
Traditional (Law, Finance, Govt, University): Conservative dress, hide
Creative (Tech, Media, Arts, Startups): More permissive on self-expression
Random Manager to check fit with culture
Check candidate is suitable and realistic
the interviewer(s) for taking the time to interview you
Do this for after every interview - make sure to write to all interviewers
Many can fail at this stage
On-site at the office (Could be o
5-8 interviews with 2-3 interviewers in each interview
Introduce yourself, small talk about weather, journey
If asked, mention you have other interviews in process
Show enthusiasm for the mission of the organization
It’s not an academic free thinking environment
Could be important for specific roles
Subject to offer, accept provisionally if you like the organization
Formal offer: can be a zoom with all interviewers
stock options mostly don’t work out
Often the improvement is stock or relocation costs (might not be worth much)
